idiom_name: Scala 3 Selectable/selectDynamic views over a Map-backed record
implementation_notes: Scala 3 makes the typed view a language feature: a class extending scala.Selectable with selectDynamic(name) turns map lookups into member selections, and the refinement in a structural type - val p: Record { val model: String } - is the view declaration, with the compiler inserting the cast that the classic pattern requires you to write. Selectable deliberately has no updateDynamic (writes go through scala.Dynamic or explicit put calls), and Selectable.WithoutPreciseParameterTypes relaxes the signature check for reflective implementations. Scala 2 can express the same idea only through structural types backed by Java reflection, which is why that path needs scala.language.reflectiveCalls and is far slower.
pitfalls: The refinement is an unchecked promise: if the map does not actually hold a String under "model", the compiler-inserted cast throws ClassCastException at the selection, exactly like the hand-written view.
selectDynamic only serves reads; assignment needs scala.Dynamic/updateDynamic or an explicit put, and Selectable reserves updateDynamic for possible future meaning, so don't define it.
Only members named in the refinement are checked - any other key still resolves at runtime through selectDynamic, so typos in one-of-a-kind reads are not caught.

variants.name: Scala 2 structural types and scala.Dynamic (reflection)
variants.implementation_notes: On Scala 2 the same idea is expressed with the scala.Dynamic trait for records you implement yourself and with reflective structural types for anything else; the compiler emits Java reflection calls, so each selection is far slower than a map lookup and an unknown member fails at runtime. Unlike Scala 3's Selectable, Dynamic does support updateDynamic, so write-through views are possible, and the language import scala.language.reflectiveCalls is required to acknowledge the dispatch cost.
variants.code_sketch:
import scala.language.dynamics

class Record(val fields: Map[String, Any]) extends Dynamic {
  def selectDynamic(name: String): Any = fields(name)   // any member, by name
}
val car = new Record(Map("model" -> "300SL"))
val view = car.asInstanceOf[Record { val model: String }]
view.model                                   // reflective call + inserted cast
pitfalls: Structural selections go through Java reflection: they need import scala.language.reflectiveCalls, are an order of magnitude slower than a Map lookup, and unknown members fail at runtime.
Scala 2 refinements allow overloads and mutable vars, which is exactly the unsoundness Scala 3 removed; code depending on it does not port forward.
